findings: Complete current MDX SHA-256 is bd84af1051d1ce4bfc12b73b979b51a76245b26da8daed7bb8ef05434d738bdf; all 7 declared sources passed current HTTPS access review.

Claims remain bounded to MRX first-party upload rules, NIST context-based information handling, FTC consumer warnings, and the stated IRS Form W-9 purpose. None is converted into a promise of confidentiality, security, fraud prevention, recipient legitimacy, or a legal or tax conclusion.

The article invents no owner, record, recipient, buyer, offer, title fact, acreage, tax result, confidentiality outcome, fraud result, testimonial, success rate, or owner-specific legal, tax, title, security, valuation, engineering, or transaction conclusion.

sources_inspected.label: Mineral Rights Xchange, Privacy Policy (accessed 2026-08-22)
sources_inspected.source_location_or_paraphrase: The MRX privacy policy says users should upload only files they are authorized to share and should not upload Social Security numbers, complete bank or payment details, passwords, or information unnecessary for the requested review. It also notes that OCR can reproduce sensitive text and that no system is perfectly secure.
sources_inspected.claim_scope: The article uses this first-party policy only to support data-minimization and authorized-sharing steps for MRX submissions; it makes no confidentiality, security, legal, or recipient-entitlement guarantee.

sources_inspected.label: Mineral Rights Xchange, Terms of Use and AI Disclosure (accessed 2026-08-22)
sources_inspected.source_location_or_paraphrase: The MRX terms require users to upload only files they are authorized to provide and to keep sign-in links secure.
sources_inspected.claim_scope: The article uses those terms only for MRX-specific authorization and access hygiene and does not infer what another recipient is legally entitled or required to receive.

sources_inspected.label: NIST SP 800-122, Guide to Protecting the Confidentiality of Personally Identifiable Information (accessed 2026-08-22)
sources_inspected.source_location_or_paraphrase: NIST SP 800-122 describes context-based identification and protection of personally identifiable information for federal information systems.
sources_inspected.claim_scope: The article uses the publication as general information-minimization context only; it does not present federal-agency guidance as governing private mineral transactions or as legal advice.

sources_inspected.label: Federal Trade Commission, How To Recognize and Avoid Phishing Scams (accessed 2026-08-22)
sources_inspected.source_location_or_paraphrase: The FTC explains that unexpected messages may seek personal or financial information and recommends contacting an organization through a known channel rather than using the message-provided path.
sources_inspected.claim_scope: The article uses that guidance only for a stop-and-confirm step before responding to an unexpected request; it does not verify or endorse a recipient, provider, or buyer.

sources_inspected.label: Federal Trade Commission, What To Know About Identity Theft (accessed 2026-08-22)
sources_inspected.source_location_or_paraphrase: The FTC provides general consumer context about misuse of personal and financial information and practical recovery resources.
sources_inspected.claim_scope: The article uses that context only to explain why unnecessary sensitive values should not be copied into a share log and does not claim that redaction prevents identity theft or other misuse.

sources_inspected.label: Internal Revenue Service, About Form W-9 (accessed 2026-08-22)
sources_inspected.source_location_or_paraphrase: The IRS states that Form W-9 is used to provide a taxpayer identification number to a person required to file an information return with the IRS.
sources_inspected.claim_scope: The article uses the page only to require a pause before changing or withholding fields on a requested tax form and makes no owner-specific tax conclusion.

sources_inspected.label: Internal Revenue Service, Form W-9 (Rev. March 2024; accessed 2026-08-22)
sources_inspected.source_location_or_paraphrase: The official Form W-9 shows that a completed form can contain a name, address, taxpayer identification number, and certification tied to its stated information-reporting purpose.
sources_inspected.claim_scope: The article uses the form only to identify why tax forms need purpose-specific instructions; it does not advise an owner to alter or withhold a required form or field.
